section_summary.extract_value: This Discussion section presents findings from a single study examining associations between positive body image (including body appreciation, body pride, body acceptance from others, and body image flexibility) and hedonic and eudaimonic well-being. The study found that body appreciation was the strongest predictor of all three indices of well-being in both women and men, and that BMI was negatively associated with well-being. Key limitations discussed include reliance on cross-sectional data, an online sample with potential recruitment bias toward women and higher education, and small sub-sample sizes of non-White participants.
